title: L. Herbert's St. Paul band: forced to play tenor
summary: He leaves Joe Cephus for Herbert's band, who wants him on tenor to replace Harry Pettiford, which goes badly.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who was this guy? He played trumpet. My memory fails me here. This guy had a little group that worked right up the street from us. I thought I would learn something by working with him, so I went with him, but I shouldn't have. I should have stayed where I was at in the first place. I was happy there and didn't realize it. L. Herbert, that's what his name was.
Yeah. He had a band in St. Paul. I was working with a cat named Joe Cephus, and I left him to go with this Al Herbert, but really he wanted me to play tenor, and shit, I wasn't no tenor player.
Had you played any reeds since you put the clarinet down?

No, I hadn't played any, but I knew how to play the tenor and I knew how to... You know, I had tried to play it, but man, like, my chops wasn't ready for the reeds. I'm used to playing on a trumpet. And it kind of held me up, you know.
He didn't want any two-trumpet group, in other words.

No, he didn't want me to play trumpet. I could out-play him playing trumpet, so he said, 'You play the saxophone.' But he had a helluva saxophone player, Harry Pettiford -- he was a helluva tenor man, you know.

And I took his place. So nobody's walking in behind that man, because that man can really play the tenor saxophone. Me, I was just learning the damn thing, hardly just about learning it. And I didn't do so good.
